title: For More Births, We Need Better Birth Experiences
gist: Amber Adrian argues that the pronatalist and pro-life agenda is really a maternal-care agenda: traumatic or coercive birth experiences are a decisive, under-measured driver of women's decisions to avoid future pregnancies, and the fix is not homebirth-vs-hospital ideology but how the birthing woman is treated. She cites Mark Cavaliere of Southwest Coalition for Life, who says ~62% of women at abortion facilities already have children and often carry unrecognized birth trauma.

themes.theme: Cultural narrative as a demand-side constraint

insights.claim: Prevailing cultural depictions render motherhood and childbirth as dramatic, negative, and frightening rather than aspirational, so pro-motherhood messaging is working against an entrenched narrative rather than a neutral one.

insights.so_what: Narrative change is a prerequisite, not a supplement, to any policy aimed at raising births.
